_README: This is a REFERENCE TEMPLATE, not a file LDO reads. A workflow has no filesystem access, so config reaches it only via args.config at invocation. Two ways to use this: (1) copy the values into your project's CLAUDE.md so Claude passes them on every run — /ldo-init writes that block for you; (2) pass them inline: Workflow({name:'ldo', args:{task:'...', config:{...}}}). Model names mean whatever your setup routes them to.
_models_note: planner is 'opus' in every tier on purpose — complexity is the Planner's own output, so it structurally can't gate its own model (only the 'medium' row's planner value is ever read at runtime). reviewer is 'opus' in trivial/medium and 'fable' in complex, falling back to 'sonnet' when fable isn't on the proxy route: catching what the coder missed is the whole point of review, and complex work has the most to miss. coder is the role that scales with the tier — haiku/sonnet/opus. reviewerFix routes review rounds 2+ and is set to the same model as reviewer in every tier, so the defaults change nothing — see _reviewerFix_note before lowering it. An override is merged per ROLE, not per tier: setting only {"medium": {"coder": "haiku"}} leaves the other six medium roles at their defaults. An unrecognised tier, role or non-string model name is warned about in the run log and ignored, never passed to the harness.
_reviewerFix_note: Round 1 is an open-ended search for defects nobody has named yet and earns the strongest model. A fix pass is a different, easier job: bounded verification of a list the previous round already wrote down. That argues for a cheaper reviewerFix — but it is a real trade, not a free saving: in a measured run, round 4 found a genuine new major that rounds 1-3 had missed. So the default is deliberately identical to reviewer, and setting reviewerFix lower is how you buy cheaper fix rounds knowing what they can cost. The post-plan log line names both models, so you can check an override took effect.
_planner_note: maxStepsPerRun is a SOFT threshold reported to the Planner, never enforced by the orchestrator — nothing is truncated, blocked, or refused above it. It tells the Planner what this project considers one run's worth of work, and above it the Planner is expected to rate fits_one_run: false unless the steps are genuinely one unit of work. preferSplit: false means 'plan it as one piece', so the Planner only flags a split when the task is incoherent as one run. Both values are interpolated into the Planner's prompt, so changing them reaches the agent doing the rating. The resulting sizing block is advisory — reported to you, never a gate.
_stallMs_note: Claude Code's stall watchdog counts only tool calls as progress, so an agent composing a large structured output (a long plan, a full verdict) looks identical to a hung one until it's already aborted. Keyed by role, not tier, because output size tracks the schema the role fills, not task complexity. recorder sits at the 180000 harness default on purpose — it runs on haiku and writes through tools, so tool_use events keep resetting its clock naturally. Values are MILLISECONDS with a floor of 1000: a seconds/ms mix-up like 480 would abort the role instantly six times in a row, so it's rejected with a warning rather than passed through.

_phases._comment: Plan, Code, and Review always run. Two are conditional.
_phases.security: runs when the Planner rates security_surface 'elevated'; force with security: true/false or securityByDefault

_securityByDefault: Not set here on purpose. Omit the key and the Planner decides (Security runs when it rates the surface 'elevated'). Add "securityByDefault": true to always threat-model, or false to never — either value overrides the Planner.
